figure: Figure 15.2, left panel ('Caching removes prefill work')
issue: The y-axis is labeled 'Prefill FLOPs / req' and the plotted formula f(r)=(S+P/r)/(S+P) treats prefill cost as linear in token counts. Prefill FLOPs are not linear in sequence length because attention contributes a quadratic term and because per-layer/fixed costs do not scale exactly with token count. The caption calls the curves illustrative but does not state the linear-cost assumption, so the figure can be read as a FLOPs model rather than a simplified token-work model.
evidence: Axis label: 'Prefill FLOPs / req (% of no-cache)'; formula: 'f(r)=(S+P/r)/(S+P)' with 'P=40%, S=60%'; caption: 'illustrative (synthetic) curves, not measured benchmarks' but no linear-cost caveat.
acceptance_test: Either relabel the y-axis to 'Relative prefill token-work (linear-cost model)' and add the linear-cost assumption to the caption/formula, or replace the formula with a cost model that includes the attention quadratic term and state the model's scope. The figure must not imply that prefill FLOPs are exactly linear in prefix/suffix length.

figure: Figure 15.2, right panel ('Decode goodput vs batch size')
issue: The drawn blue curve is nearly linear on the log batch-size axis and does not visibly show the 'diminishing gains past ~b16' or the approach to HBM-bandwidth saturation claimed by the annotation and caption. The post-16 segment rises at least as steeply as the pre-16 segment, so the visual encoding contradicts the stated mechanism.
evidence: Annotation: 'diminishing gains past ~b16 (no hard plateau): goodput still rises; tail latency keeps rising'; caption: 'rising with diminishing gains as HBM bandwidth approaches saturation (the illustrative curve does not reach a hard plateau)'. The plotted points from batch 16 to 64 continue upward with no visible reduction in slope on the log x-axis.
acceptance_test: Redraw the curve so the post-b16 slope visibly decreases toward an asymptote (e.g., a concave-down saturation curve), or change the annotation/caption to describe the drawn curve as log-linear illustrative growth rather than saturation. The figure and caption must agree on the shape.

issue: The legend entries '$20.80/1K' and '$15–25/1K' do not specify whether '1K' means 1K requests or 1K tokens. The caption uses '$20.80 per 1M tokens (≈$0.0208 per 1K-token request)' and the prose uses '$20.8/1K' as a per-1K-request rate. A reader can interpret the legend as $20.80 per 1K tokens, which is 1000× the intended slope and would make the managed line and break-even region wrong.
evidence: Legend: 'managed $20.80/1K'; 'price band $15–25/1K'. Caption: '$20.80 per 1M tokens (≈$0.0208 per 1K-token request) API'; prose on printed p. 267: 'the canonical-price point at $20.8/1K is 7,491,198.56 ≈ 7.5M'.
acceptance_test: Change the legend to an unambiguous unit, e.g. '$20.80 per 1K requests (≈$0.0208/request)' or '$20.80 per 1M tokens at 1K tokens/request', and make the price-band legend use the same basis. The legend, caption, and prose must all state the same denominator.

issue: The x-axis label says 'duration varied at FIXED 40 rps peak, FIXED 21-host fleet', but the vertical 'feasible max 24.96M' line assumes the canonical 624,000 active-s/mo duty cycle. If the reader interprets 'duration varied' as varying the active window, the fixed feasible-max line appears inconsistent. The caption and printed p. 268 clarify that only load duration within the fixed active window varies, but the axis label alone is ambiguous.
evidence: X-axis label: 'Requests/month (log) — duration varied at FIXED 40 rps peak, FIXED 21-host fleet'; annotation: 'feasible max 24.96M'; caption: 'feasible max = capacity 40 rps × 624,000 s = 24.96M req/mo'; printed p. 268: 'only how long the peak-shaped load runs inside the active window moves along x'.
acceptance_test: Revise the x-axis label to make the fixed active window explicit, e.g. 'Requests/month (log) — load duration varied within the fixed 624,000 s active window; 40 rps peak; 21-host fleet'. Alternatively, if the active window is meant to vary, replace the single feasible-max line with a duration-dependent bound.
